country.evidence_source: To our knowledge, this is the first U.K.-based study to investigate prospective relationships between perceived sex discrimination and mental health and well-being outcomes.

Outcome_variable.evidence_source: Possible scores on psychological distress, measured with the General Health Questionnaire, range from 0 to 12; possible scores on mental functioning, measured with the 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-12), range from 0 to 100; and possible life satisfaction scores range from 0 to 7.

sample_type.evidence_source: current study adds to the cross-sectional literature by demonstrating these relationships in a large U.K. sample, as previous work was dominated by small, convenience samples of university students and employees in the United States.

ethnicity.evidence_source: All analyses are adjusted for age, household income, education, and ethnicity.

lag.evidence_source: In this U.S. sample, no significant relationships between sex discrimination and loneliness, mental well-being and life satisfaction at 4-year follow-up were observed (Sutin et al., 2015).
